licences.notes: Words as printed in the Schirmer vocal score (giacche and fo without accents, Bricconaccia, Cavaliera with a capital; the libretto has già che or giacchè, fo/fò and Briconaccia).

licences.source: G. Schirmer vocal score, New York 1900 (plate 15147, IMSLP #68957), pages 58–61, bars 1–96 of No. 6
licences.author: G. Schirmer, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: the sung line and the piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, then checked bar by bar and checked again by a fresh checker. The English singing translation and the stage directions are left out; Don Giovanni, Zerlina and Leporello are on stage but do not sing. The time signature is a plain C (4/4), not alla breve. Where the print slurs the piano's recurring tied left-hand chords both above and below, only the lower slur is kept. Playback tempo: Allegro di molto ♩ = 235 (a half note ≈ 118), about 1:38, from the median (1:38) of five complete recordings (Fricsay 1958 1:35, Giulini 1959 1:38, Böhm 1977 1:38, Haitink 1984 1:37, Karajan 1985 1:38). Mozart gives the words only.
